chapter.title: Federal Hospitality
chapter.goal: Steve wants to hand the problem to someone in charge.

c4_safe.objective: Find out whether the man in charge is really Adrian Rook.
notes: record becomes a rows puzzle (drop the case board). screens keeps the case board with one stage and decoys.
The karaoke beat and ‘Adrian hates karaoke’ come from the character bible (the real Rook hates karaoke; the copy is very good at it).
Rook’s notebook question pays off Interlude 1, where the Archivist’s report says ‘Engine details in subject’s notebook’.
Walt Prior on the placements list pays off Chapter 3.
context: steve|Adrian Rook arrived the next afternoon with four agents and two black SUVs. He was everything June had promised. Calm. Kind. Thorough.
steve|He drove us to a safe house in the Coast Range, three hours from anywhere.
steve|I kept thinking about that text. If someone wanted to cut me off from the one man who could help, that’s exactly what they’d send.
steve|On the drive, every station talked about President Ward. On November seventh she signs an accord with China at Sentinel Point.
intro: rook_copy|One more thing, Steve. Your mother kept a notebook. Any idea where?
steve|Mom kept a lot of notebooks.

intro.new: steve|He had already taken every tape I’d brought. Not Mom’s voicemail. That cassette lives in my cardigan pocket, and I didn’t offer it.

record.title: Rook’s office door
record.goal: Get a clean take of Rook’s line to compare with June’s voicemail.
record.background: June keeps Rook’s voicemail on her phone: “Sit tight, June.” Every hour Rook goes on hold with ‘the Bureau’. When the hold music stops, he leans out and says the same words to her. The karaoke machine is in the lounge. June’s window is next to the loud generator. Rook’s office door has a gap at the bottom.

lead.new: steve|Every hour, on the hour, Rook goes on hold with the Bureau. And he hums along.
lead.sfx: hold music through the office door

lead: steve|When the music stops, he leans out and tells June the same thing. Word for word, like the voicemail on her phone.
calder|If you record Adrian, Mercer, I want to hear this house around his voice. Not my phone.
steve|The lounge has the karaoke machine, and the generator roars right under June’s window.
steve|But his office door has a gap at the bottom. And he speaks a second after the music stops.
record.prompt: Where should Steve record, when should he press the button, and what should he keep?
record.instruction: Find a quiet spot close to Rook, start before his first word, and keep proof that the take was made in this house.
hints: Get close to Rook, away from the singing and the generator.
Rook speaks right after the music stops. If Steve starts late, he clips the first word.
June wants to hear this house around Rook’s words. Which version still has the room in it?
lines: c4_safe.record.01
c4_safe.record.02
record.finding: steve|I have Rook’s line on Dad’s tape, from outside his door, with this house’s room sound around it. Nobody can say I copied it off June’s phone.

match.title: Two takes
match.goal: Compare Rook’s voice through the door with June’s voicemail.
match.background: On Sunday, Nora’s good morning came out the same, breath for breath, on two different days. People never say a line exactly the same way twice. A recording always does.
lead: calder|You want my voicemail? Mercer, that’s a federal agent you’re recording.
steve|Then it won’t matter. Please, June.
steve|Remember Nora’s good morning? Two days, same breath, same pause. People never do that. Recordings do.
match.prompt: Play June’s voicemail and Steve’s take from the door. What do you hear?
options: Rook saying it again, more slowly
A shorter cut of the voicemail

wrong.0: The pace is the same. Every pause lands in exactly the same place.
wrong.2: Nothing is missing. Both takes start and end on the same breath.

hints: Follow the small sounds too: the breath, the little click on the S.
If a man said it twice, something would move: a breath, a pause, the click. Nothing moves.

lines.text: Different rooms. Same breath, same pause, same little click on the S. That isn’t a man repeating himself. That’s a recording wearing a man.

lines: calder|Play it again.
match.finding: steve|June’s voicemail and Rook’s voice through the door are one recording, breath for breath, like Nora’s good morning. The man running this house isn’t Adrian Rook.

screens.title: Rook’s monitor wall
screens.goal: Find out what Rook’s office is really watching.
screens.background: Rook’s office has a wall of screens the Bureau never installed. A label on the rack reads GALLERY. In the aquarium, Steve learned that a picture looping the same cough on the same beat had nobody in it. The papers in Rook’s drawer name the beds.

lead.new: steve|That night the agents dragged out the karaoke machine. Rook sang three songs. Beautifully.

lead: calder|Adrian hates karaoke. He walked out of my wedding when the machine came on.
calder|...Odd behavior proves nothing. My own rule.
steve|While he was singing, his office door was open.
steve|In the aquarium, a picture that kept repeating meant nobody was really there.
screens.prompt: Which feed is live, and who are the beds for?

board.instruction: Use the screens and the papers in the drawer to answer each question.
evidence: Feeds 1, 2 and 4 show the same attendant limping past every forty seconds, coughing on the same step.
On feed 3, a frosted bed cracks open and seals again, and nobody walks past.
The bed nearest the camera on feed 3 is tagged 41B.
The roster in the drawer says: Bed 41B, Adrian Rook, FBI.
A transfer sheet with both governments’ seals says: Bed 42B, President Ward, signing day.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.

board.wrong_text: Steve looks again. Something here doesn’t match the screens or the papers yet.

hints: Feeds 1, 2 and 4 loop every forty seconds. Read the bed tag on the feed that doesn’t.
Match the live feed’s bed tag to the roster. The transfer sheet names the other bed.

lines.text: Adrian Rook, asleep in bed 41B. Both governments’ seals on the transfer. And an empty bed waiting for President Ward on signing day.

lines: steve|And a list of placements in Washington and Beijing. The first name on it is Walt, from June’s list.
screens.finding: steve|The real Adrian Rook is asleep on that ship, in bed 41B. They have people in Washington and in Beijing. And they’ve made up a bed for President Ward, for the day she signs the accord.

recap: steve|Rook’s voice is a recording. The real Rook is asleep under the bay. And there’s a bed waiting for the President.
steve|I had to tell June. Rook had made sure I couldn’t just walk down the hall and do it.

outro.new: rook_copy|June will sit with my team in the east wing tonight. You’ll be more comfortable in the west.

outro: rook_copy|And Steve. The notebook. Anything at all you remember.

lines: steve|Who is looking after Biscuit while you’re up here?
calder|Dale. He comes by twice a day with the mail anyway.
calder|She likes him better than me. He never forgets the treats.
calder|My father brought me up here to fish when I was a girl. We never caught a thing.
steve|Then why did you keep coming?
calder|For the sandwiches. And three whole hours where nobody could phone him.
calder|Adrian and I worked a case together twenty years ago. He argued with everyone, including me.
steve|He hasn’t argued with anybody since he got here.
calder|No. He hasn’t. I noticed that too.
steve|Nice place. Does the Bureau own it?
rook_copy|It does. Every room is exactly as the file describes. I checked them all twice.
steve|You read the file on the furniture?
rook_copy|I read everything, Steve. It saves time later.
steve|June says you take your coffee with three sugars.
rook_copy|I take it however the house makes it.
steve|That isn’t really an answer.
rook_copy|It’s a very good answer. It never disappoints anyone.

c4_escape.objective: Get the proof to June, then get out of the house.
changes: critic C21 (simplified to a rows choice)
notes: No small talk here: Steve is alone in the service wing, and June is only heard on tape.
June’s reply comes back through the tube on Dad’s recorder, so her lines are recorded_playback. Steve does not see her again until Chapter 6.
van becomes a rows puzzle (drop the case board). The escort’s radio, which Steve takes with him, carries Rook’s orders in the departure.
context: steve|Rook put June in the east wing and me in the west, with an agent at each end of the hall. Kindly. Firmly.
steve|The house was older than the FBI. In the service corridor, there were brass tubes in the wall.

tube.title: Pneumatic post
tube.goal: Get the warning and both recordings to June without passing Rook’s desk.
tube.background: June is in the east wing. The old brass tubes still run between rooms, and a diverter panel picks the room. The panel uses the builders’ room names, not numbers. June was moved out of OAK tonight. She believes what she can hear for herself.
lead: steve|Pneumatic post. Dad would have loved this.
steve|If both takes reach June, she can hear it for herself. Rook’s desk sorts everything else.
steve|The night list says June moved out of OAK, into the room across from the linen cupboard.
steve|Standard capsules stop at Rook’s desk for sorting. The blue maintenance ones go straight through.
tube.prompt: Which room, which capsule, and what goes inside?
tube.instruction: Send the capsule straight to June’s new room, with something she can hear for herself. The builder’s sketch shows ALDER opposite the linen cupboard and PINE facing the lift.
hints: June isn’t in her first room any more.
Find the linen cupboard on the builder’s sketch. Then think about who opens the standard capsules.
June won’t act on a note alone. She trusts her own ears, and she needs both takes to compare.

lines.text: I heard both. I’ll keep his attention. You get out. We both know you can’t bluff him in person.
lines.direction: the capsule comes back with Dad’s recorder; June has recorded a reply at the end of the tape

lines.new: steve|Nobody had asked me for that since the funeral.

tube.finding: steve|June heard both takes, and she believes me. She’s staying with Rook to keep him busy. I have to get myself out.

fault.title: Safety test panel
fault.goal: Get the west corridor moved out of the house, while June keeps Rook in the east wing.
fault.background: The safe house has a fire-drill console run from coloured cards. The drill ticket is signed by the van escort, who works in the west corridor. The west corridor holds Steve and three agents. Rook and June are in the front office, in the east wing.
lead: steve|A drill console. If a drill says the west wing has to go, they’ll have to move me. In a van.
steve|Yesterday’s log says what each card does. SILVER moves the signer. BLUE moves his whole corridor. WHITE moves everyone else.
steve|The van escort signed tonight’s ticket, and he works my corridor. Four of us sleep on the west side.
fault.prompt: Which card, which mode, and where should the west team meet?
fault.instruction: Move the whole west corridor for real, to a place with four seats away from Rook. A dry run only prints the route. A floor rehearsal moves people. The covered court seats three, the transport bay seats four, and Rook is using the front office.
hints: Who signed the ticket, and which corridor does he work in?
Only one card moves the signer’s whole corridor. Only one mode moves anyone at all.
Count the west team. Then find a place with enough seats where Rook isn’t.
lines: c4_escape.fault.01
fault.finding: steve|A BLUE drill, for real, on the escort’s own ticket. The whole west corridor, me included, goes to the transport bay. Rook stays in the east wing with June.

van.title: Transport van
van.goal: Get out of the moving van at the one moment the door will open.
van.background: Steve is in the back of the van with one escort. The rear handle only works while the travel catch is off. At the drill briefing the escort explained the rule: the catch comes off when the driver radios ‘slowing for gravel’, and goes back on at the next stop.
lead: steve|One escort. One rear door. And a catch that only comes off for gravel.
steve|The driver radios before he slows. First a brick bridge over the canal, then a gravel bend.
steve|After the gravel comes the weighbridge. There, the escort opens the door himself.
van.prompt: When should Steve pull the handle, and which way should he jump?
van.instruction: Pull the handle while the catch is off, and jump toward the softer side. On the gravel bend, the right side drops into a soft ditch, and the left side is a rock face.
hints: The handle only works while the catch is off.
The catch only comes off for gravel. Check which side is soft.
The brick bridge has no gravel, and at the weighbridge the escort opens the door himself. A ditch is softer than rock.
lines: c4_escape.van.01
van.finding: steve|On the gravel bend, with the catch off, I pulled the handle and jumped for the soft side. Mostly I fell. But I fell out of the van, with the escort’s radio in my hand.

recap: steve|June has the proof, and she chose to stay with Rook so I could run.
steve|Now I was in a ditch in the Coast Range with Dad’s recorder, a stolen radio and no plan. And the radio was still talking.

outro.text: All units. Steve Mercer, wanted for the abduction of Nora Reyes. And scan Calder tonight. The signing is in six days.
Kidnapping Nora. They took her, and I’m the one on the poster. I have to keep moving.
